about: Every Maestro Pro guide, grouped. Each page has an HTML url and a Markdown url.

topics.title: Getting Started
topics.summary: Maestro Pro is a working tool for musicians: it reads your scores and follows them to the note, turns pages hands-free, rehearses with a backing track, a song from Apple Music, the built-in instrument or a metronome, and lets you write and revise the music itself.

children.title: What Maestro Pro is
children.summary: Maestro Pro is an app for musicians that reads your scores, follows them to the note and plays along.

children.title: Your first minute
children.summary: Import a score, press Play and tap the music to start from any point.

children.title: Open the sample score
children.summary: Try the app straight away with the built-in sample, no files needed.

children.title: Find free scores with Search Scores
children.summary: Search Scores downloads classical pieces and jazz tunes, and searches the web for free scores.

children.title: What the Free plan includes
children.summary: The Free plan keeps up to three scores and lets you view and play them, with some tools left for paid plans.

topics.title: Your Library
topics.summary: Everything you import lives in the library and stays on the device. It is also kept in iCloud when iCloud Drive is on.

children.title: Supported file types
children.summary: PDF, MusicXML, MIDI, karaoke, lyrics, CD+Graphics and Maestro Pro files can all be imported.

children.title: Import a score
children.summary: Tap Import Score, choose your files, and they appear in the library.

children.title: Import a PDF score
children.summary: PDFs are read by the app, which only reads printed notation, and scans need to be straight and clear.

children.title: Import MusicXML files
children.summary: MusicXML files (.musicxml, .xml, .mxl) import like any other score and can be edited.

children.title: Import MIDI and karaoke files
children.summary: MIDI and karaoke (.mid, .kar) files import with Import Score; karaoke files carry their own words.

children.title: Import several files at once
children.summary: Choose more than one file in the import dialog and they all arrive together.

children.title: Drag files onto the window
children.summary: Drag files from the Files app straight onto the Maestro Pro window to import them.

children.title: Import from another app's share sheet
children.summary: Choose Maestro Pro in the share sheet of Files, Mail, Safari, Messages and other apps.

children.title: Import a whole folder
children.summary: Import Folder reads every supported file in a folder.

children.title: Link a folder to the library
children.summary: In Settings, Link a Folder keeps a folder in step with the library so new files appear by themselves.

children.title: Start a blank score
children.summary: New Blank Score creates an empty score with the name, time signature, key, bars, staves and tempo you choose.

children.title: Lyrics with Backing
children.summary: Choose a backing track and the app finds its timed lyrics online for a karaoke-style screen.

children.title: Keep your library in iCloud
children.summary: Your library is stored on the device and is also kept in iCloud when iCloud Drive is on.

children.title: Set-lists for rehearsals and gigs
children.summary: Build set-lists for a lesson, a rehearsal or a concert.

children.title: Band-in-a-Box files
children.summary: Band-in-a-Box files cannot be read; export MusicXML and audio from Band-in-a-Box instead.

topics.title: Playing a Score
topics.summary: The bar at the bottom controls playback; the toolbar and the Inspector change how it looks and sounds.

children.title: Play, pause and skip
children.summary: The bar at the bottom has Play and Pause, skip by bar and a progress bar you can drag.

children.title: Start from any bar
children.summary: Tap the music to jump to that point, or drag the progress bar.

children.title: Playback keys on a Mac
children.summary: Space plays and pauses, arrows skip bars, Return goes to the start and K toggles the metronome.

children.title: Slow down or speed up without changing pitch
children.summary: Practice Speed runs from 10 to 400 percent and keeps the pitch the same.

children.title: Tempo and Custom Tempo
children.summary: The tempo is the score's own unless you set one; Custom Tempo goes back to the score's.

children.title: Tap the tempo
children.summary: Tap the tempo, then tap the Tap key in time with the beat and the tempo follows you.

children.title: Loop a hard passage
children.summary: In the Inspector, Loop plays the bars you choose over and over.

children.title: Count In and Lead-in Bars
children.summary: Count In plays a bar of clicks first; Lead-in Bars sets how many bars of introduction come before bar 1.

children.title: Use the metronome
children.summary: The metronome clicks on every beat and can be turned on and off, with K on a Mac.

children.title: Transpose for your instrument
children.summary: Transposing typesets the score again in the new key, rather than just labelling it.

children.title: Set your instrument
children.summary: Setting your instrument to B flat or E flat in the Inspector shows the written note in the tuner.

children.title: Automatic page turning
children.summary: The page scrolls or curls over like a real book exactly when you need it.

children.title: Notes and bars that light up
children.summary: Notes glow as they sound and a soft wash marks the bar; this needs the Performer plan or above.

children.title: The Inspector
children.summary: The Inspector holds tempo, practice speed, loop, key, instrument and backing tracks.

children.title: Turn pages and start playback with a pedal
children.summary: Give a MIDI pedal a job in Settings, Listening; a Bluetooth page turner works with no setting up.

topics.title: Plans and pricing
topics.summary: Free, Performer and Professional: what each plan includes, and how to buy.

children.title: The Free plan
children.summary: What you get for nothing: up to three scores, viewing, lyrics files, your own audio, GitHub and scales.

children.title: The Performer plan
children.summary: Everything except the score editor, with a library of any size.

children.title: The Professional plan
children.summary: Everything, including the score editor, medleys and version history with GitHub sync.

children.title: Which plan do I need?
children.summary: A quick way to choose between Free, Performer and Professional.

children.title: Buy Professional on this website
children.summary: Pay monthly or yearly on the website, then recover your licence key and install the app.

children.title: Website or in-app: which is cheaper?
children.summary: Professional bought on the website costs less than Performer bought in the app, and includes the editor.

children.title: Prices and currencies
children.summary: Website prices are in pounds sterling or the local equivalent, and app prices show in your own currency.

children.title: Manage a subscription bought in the app
children.summary: Performer and Professional bought in the app are managed in your Apple Account settings.

topics.title: Licences and keys
topics.summary: How your licence key works, how to enter it and what to do if you lose it.

children.title: Enter your licence key in the app
children.summary: On the paywall, tap Already have a licence key? and type your key.

children.title: Recover a lost licence key
children.summary: Enter the email address you paid with and the key is emailed to you.

children.title: Manage your licence in the app
children.summary: With a licence key, Settings shows Manage Licence: remove a device or request a cancellation.

children.title: Use your licence on up to 3 devices
children.summary: A licence bought on the website works on up to 3 devices. Education licences have no limit.

children.title: Remove a device from your licence
children.summary: Use the devices page on the key page to see where your licence is used and remove a device.

children.title: If you have more than one licence key
children.summary: If you have subscribed more than once, the email lists every active key with its plan.

children.title: My licence key is not working
children.summary: Check the key, check it is still active, and recover it again if needed.

topics.title: Install with TestFlight
topics.summary: Maestro Pro is installed through Apple's TestFlight app until it reaches the App Store.

children.title: Install Maestro Pro step by step
children.summary: Install TestFlight, accept the invitation, install Maestro Pro, then enter your key.

children.title: I lost the TestFlight link
children.summary: The key email includes the TestFlight link, and the install page has it too.

topics.title: Refunds and cancellation
topics.summary: The 14-day money-back guarantee, and how to cancel a licence bought on the website.

children.title: The 14-day money-back guarantee
children.summary: Ask for a full refund within 14 days of your first payment, once the payment has cleared.

children.title: How to request a refund or cancel
children.summary: Use the cancellation page with your licence key and follow the steps.

children.title: Refunds for subscriptions bought in the app
children.summary: If you subscribed inside the app through the App Store, Apple handles the refund, not us.

children.title: When can I get a refund?
children.summary: Refunds are made from day 8 to day 14 after the first payment, once it has cleared.

children.title: Cancelling after the 14 days
children.summary: No refund, but you can cancel going forward, and how that works differs for yearly and monthly plans.

children.title: Cancel a yearly licence
children.summary: Your yearly subscription is cancelled and the key works until the end of the year you paid for.

children.title: Cancel a monthly licence
children.summary: Monthly licences are on a 12-month contract, so cancelling early costs one month plus half of the remaining term.

topics.title: Education and schools
topics.summary: How schools, colleges and tutors can get Maestro Pro, including volume licensing outside the App Store.

children.title: Apple volume purchasing
children.summary: Schools can roll the free version out through Apple School Manager or Apple Business Manager.

children.title: Buy for a whole organisation
children.summary: One licence for unlimited students and teachers, £499 a year, bought direct and outside the App Store.

children.title: The student licence
children.summary: Students can buy Professional for £48 a year or £6 a month on a 12-month contract.

topics.title: Tuner & Wait for Me
topics.summary: Maestro Pro can listen through the microphone: to tune your instrument, to train a steady note, and to wait for you to play a score note by note. Sound is analysed on the device and is never recorded or sent anywhere.

children.title: Open the tuner
children.summary: The Tuner is on the home screen, the + menu, Settings under Listening, and the tuning fork in a score's toolbar.

children.title: Read the tuner display
children.summary: It shows the note name, how many cents sharp or flat you are, and the frequency, with a needle and an eight-second trace.

children.title: Play a reference note
children.summary: Play Reference Note sounds the note you are aiming for.

children.title: Change the tuning pitch (A = 440 Hz)
children.summary: A = 440 Hz can be changed between 415 and 466 for baroque or orchestral tuning.

children.title: Tune a B flat or E flat instrument
children.summary: With your instrument set to B flat or E flat in the Inspector, the tuner shows the written note too.

children.title: What is Wait for Me?
children.summary: Wait for Me holds the score until the right note is played in tune.

children.title: Follow a MIDI instrument instead of the microphone
children.summary: With a MIDI instrument connected, Wait for Me and Record follow the keys you press instead of listening through the microphone.

children.title: Chords and both hands in Wait for Me by MIDI
children.summary: With a MIDI instrument, Wait for Me wants every note of a chord, and can ask for both staves of a piano score at once.

children.title: The steady-note trainer
children.summary: A trainer that listens as you hold a note steady, alongside the tuner and Wait for Me.

topics.title: Record & Review
topics.summary: Record yourself playing a score, then review the take with the notes lit: green where you should have been, red where you actually were. It listens through the microphone, so it works with any instrument or your voice.

children.title: Record yourself
children.summary: Press Record, play along after the count-in, then press Stop.

children.title: Record when the score has a backing track
children.summary: The app asks first, because the microphone would hear the backing: Mute It and Record, or Record Anyway.

children.title: Review your take
children.summary: The take is shown with the notes lit: green where you should have been, red where you actually were.

children.title: Where recordings are kept
children.summary: Recordings are kept with the score, copied when you duplicate it, and compressed to well under a megabyte a minute.

topics.title: Scales & Arpeggios
topics.summary: Practice material made on demand.

children.title: Make a scale or arpeggio
children.summary: Choose Scales & Arpeggios on the home screen, pick the kind and a key, and a score is created for you.

children.title: Scale types and keys
children.summary: Major, minor, blues, arpeggios and more, in any key.

children.title: Scales are free on every plan
children.summary: Making scales and arpeggios in any key is included on the Free plan too.

topics.title: Annotating
topics.summary: Mark up the page like a paper part.

children.title: Draw on a score
children.summary: Turn on Annotate in the toolbar and draw; the ink is saved with the score and shows while you play.

children.title: Annotation tools
children.summary: Pens, markers, pencil, colours and an eraser.

children.title: Annotations and zoom
children.summary: Each zoom size keeps its own drawing so it stays lined up with the music.

children.title: Annotate on a Mac
children.summary: On a Mac you draw with the trackpad or mouse instead of Apple Pencil.

children.title: Export and print with your ink
children.summary: Export as PDF and Print include your ink for the key and zoom you are viewing.

topics.title: Backing Tracks & Sound
topics.summary: A backing track is a recording that plays with the score. The built-in instrument can play the notes on the page too.

children.title: Play the score through a MIDI instrument
children.summary: Settings, Playback, Play Through MIDI Instrument sends the notes to your keyboard or sound module.

children.title: Add a backing track
children.summary: Add the first backing track with Add Backing Track, and it plays in time with the score.

children.title: Add more than one backing track
children.summary: A score can have several tracks, for example a rhythm section and a separate guide vocal.

children.title: Track switches and levels
children.summary: Each track has its own switch and its own level from minus 24 to plus 12 decibels.

children.title: The first track keeps time
children.summary: The first backing track is the one the score keeps time with; later tracks follow its speed and key.

children.title: Match Key and Tempo to a track
children.summary: Match Key & Tempo works on the first backing track; use it again if the track starts late or early.

children.title: Reduce vocals on a track
children.summary: Reduce Vocals cuts the singer down in a stereo recording; it cannot remove a voice from a mono recording.

children.title: Play along with Apple Music
children.summary: Play a song from your Apple Music subscription alongside a score and see its lyrics.

children.title: The built-in instrument
children.summary: The built-in instrument can play the notes on the page, as can a metronome.

children.title: Equaliser and key changes
children.summary: Key changes and the equaliser are part of the Performer and Professional plans.

topics.title: Lyrics & Karaoke
topics.summary: Lyrics scroll in time with the music like in Apple Music, and CD+Graphics karaoke files show their built-in pictures.

children.title: Add a lyrics file
children.summary: Add a .lrc file (timed lines) or a .txt file to a score from the Lyrics menu.

children.title: Show lyrics instead of music
children.summary: Show Lyrics Instead of Music swaps the page for the words, which scroll in time like Apple Music.

children.title: Animate syllables
children.summary: Animate Syllables swells each syllable as it is sung, and Show Syllable Progress fills it.

children.title: Lyrics typeface, size and blur
children.summary: Typeface, size, alignment and blur for lines not being sung are set in Settings.

children.title: Lyrics-only items
children.summary: A lyrics-only item has its own screen with a transport bar and an optional backing track.

children.title: Lyrics in seconds or in bars
children.summary: When a lyrics file has no timing, you can choose whether lyrics are timed in seconds or in bars.

children.title: Karaoke MIDI (.kar) files
children.summary: Karaoke MIDI files contain their own words.

children.title: CD+Graphics karaoke (.cdg)
children.summary: CD+Graphics karaoke files show their built-in pictures.

children.title: Find lyrics and singers online
children.summary: Lyrics and singers can be found online; this needs the internet and sends the song title and artist to lyric services.

children.title: Duets and singers
children.summary: Duets get a singer each, in their own colour.

topics.title: Writing & Editing Music
topics.summary: The score editor changes the notes in a MusicXML score. A PDF is first read by the app, and the editor works on a copy of what it read. Open it with Edit Score (the music-note-list button; in Simple mode it appears for scores you created).

children.title: Open the score editor
children.summary: Edit Score opens the editor, which works on MusicXML scores and on a copy of what the app read from a PDF.

children.title: The nine editor modes
children.summary: One strip of nine modes at the bottom of the editor: Notes, Rests, Marks, Dynamics, Bars, Form, Medley, Erase and Draw.

children.title: Notes mode: add and move notes
children.summary: Slide on a rest to choose a pitch, lift to place a note, drag to move one, scribble to rub it out.

children.title: Rests mode
children.summary: Turn a note into a rest, change a rest's length, or take a rest off the page.

children.title: Marks mode: accidentals, ties and articulations
children.summary: Add a sharp, flat or natural, tie notes, or give a note staccato, accent, tenuto, marcato or a fermata.

children.title: Dynamics mode
children.summary: Put dynamics from ppp to fff on a note or bar, and crescendo or diminuendo hairpins over bars.

children.title: Bars mode: repeats, adding and deleting bars
children.summary: Repeat signs, adding a bar before or after, deleting one or several bars, and Expand Repeats to write a piece out as it is played.

children.title: The touch and hold menu
children.summary: Touch and hold a note, rest or bar in the editor for a menu of what you can do to it.

children.title: Form mode: endings, jumps and tempo marks
children.summary: First and second time bars, Segno, Coda, To Coda, D.C., D.S., Fine and tempo marks.

children.title: Medley mode: copy, cut and paste bars
children.summary: Drag across bars to choose them, then Copy, Cut, Paste, Duplicate or Delete, or Insert from Score.

children.title: Erase mode
children.summary: Touch or drag over notes and rests to erase them; double-tap Apple Pencil to switch to the eraser.

children.title: Draw mode
children.summary: Write over the music with Apple Pencil using pen, marker, pencil and colour tools; the ink stays on the page.

children.title: Beats per bar
children.summary: Options has Beats per Bar: 4, 3 or a custom number, chosen to match the score when the editor opens.

children.title: Edit a score that came from a PDF
children.summary: The app first reads a PDF, and the editor works on a copy of what it read.

children.title: Stop a resting hand changing notes
children.summary: The setting Edit with Apple Pencil Only stops a resting hand changing notes.

children.title: Guitar tab: read any staff as tablature
children.summary: Any staff can be shown as guitar tablature: fret numbers on six string lines, with the rhythm on stems underneath.

children.title: Write and edit guitar tab
children.summary: On a tab staff, touch a string to put in its open note, then use the Fret buttons; drag a note to another string.

children.title: Write notes on the on-screen piano keyboard
children.summary: The piano keys button in the score editor shows a keyboard; tap keys to write notes one after another while the bars being written stay at the top.

children.title: Write notes with a MIDI keyboard or instrument
children.summary: Plug a MIDI instrument into an iPad or Mac and play: each note is written at the selection in the score editor, and held keys make chords.

children.title: Tab tunings, bass, ukulele and capo
children.summary: Give a tab staff another tuning (Drop D, DADGAD, Open G, bass, ukulele) or a capo from the staff's menu.

children.title: Hammer-ons, pull-offs, slides, bends and palm mutes
children.summary: In Marks mode, a note on tab has buttons for Hammer-On, Pull-Off, Slide, Bend and Palm Mute.

children.title: Show notes with tab underneath
children.summary: Guitar Tab Underneath prints a staff's music a second time as tab, and both stay in step.

children.title: Write chord symbols and show guitar chord diagrams
children.summary: In Marks mode, tap Chord to write a chord over a note; Chords on the Page shows names or names with guitar diagrams.

children.title: Write two voices on one staff
children.summary: Add Second Voice gives a bar a second row of rests to write a second rhythm on the same staff.
keywords: melody and accompaniment on one staff

children.title: Record what you play into the score, in time
children.summary: Tap Record in the score editor and play a MIDI instrument to the metronome; the notes are written with their rhythm.

topics.title: Version History & GitHub
topics.summary: Save versions of a score, try ideas on branches, merge them back, and keep it all on GitHub.

children.title: Save a version
children.summary: In the score editor, History and Save Version keep a snapshot you can return to.

children.title: Start a branch to try an idea
children.summary: New Branch starts a separate line of edits from now or from any earlier version.

children.title: Roll back to an earlier version
children.summary: Roll Back to This Version restores an earlier snapshot as a new version, so nothing is lost.

children.title: Merge a branch
children.summary: Merge brings another branch into the current one, bar by bar.

children.title: Resolve merge clashes
children.summary: A bar changed on both branches clashes, and you choose to keep yours or take theirs.

children.title: Connect a score to GitHub
children.summary: Connect a score to your own GitHub repository and push its version history there.

children.title: Where your GitHub token is kept
children.summary: The token is kept in your device's Keychain and sent only to GitHub.

topics.title: Share, Export & Print
topics.summary: Get a score, or a video of it, out of the app.

children.title: Export as MusicXML
children.summary: MusicXML opens in MuseScore, Finale, Sibelius, Dorico, Notion and most other notation apps.

children.title: Export as a MIDI file
children.summary: Share, Export as MIDI saves the notes as a standard MIDI file for any other music program.

children.title: Export as PDF
children.summary: A PDF score is passed on as it is; any other score is typeset in the key currently shown.

children.title: Print a score
children.summary: Print opens the system print dialog.

children.title: The Share menu
children.summary: Press and hold a score in the library and choose Share for Export as MusicXML, Export as PDF and Print.

children.title: Save to Files, AirDrop, email or message
children.summary: In the share sheet you can save to Files, AirDrop, email or message the file.

children.title: Get a video of a score
children.summary: A video of the music following along can be taken out of the app.

topics.title: Play Together
topics.summary: Up to eight devices running Maestro Pro can play in time with each other (Advanced mode).

children.title: Start a Play Together session
children.summary: Open your parts, choose Play Together, then Start a Session, and allow each player in.

children.title: Join a session
children.summary: Choose Join a Session and pick the host's device.

children.title: Local Network permission
children.summary: Allow the Local Network permission if asked; devices find each other over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, with no account.

children.title: Nudge for wireless speakers and headphones
children.summary: The Nudge slider moves your sound earlier or later if you use wireless speakers or headphones.

children.title: Using Play Together in lessons and rehearsals
children.summary: Play, pause, seek and tempo changes on any device are mirrored on all of them.

topics.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
topics.summary: On a Mac nearly everything has a keyboard shortcut, shown in the Playback, Score and View menus. On an iPad with a keyboard, hold the Command key to see them. Every shortcut can be changed.

children.title: See the keyboard shortcuts
children.summary: On a Mac shortcuts are shown in the Playback, Score and View menus; on an iPad hold the Command key.

children.title: Change a shortcut
children.summary: In Settings under Keyboard Shortcuts, click a shortcut and press the keys you want instead.

children.title: Put shortcuts back
children.summary: The arrow beside a shortcut resets it, and Reset All to Defaults resets them all.

topics.title: Settings & Accessibility
topics.summary: Settings has the choices that apply everywhere.

children.title: Open the guide and support from the app
children.summary: Settings has Guide and Support buttons that open this website inside the app.

children.title: Light, dark or system appearance
children.summary: Appearance is light, dark, or follows the system.

children.title: Highlight colour
children.summary: Highlight Colour chooses the colour that lights up playing notes; the toolbar uses your accent colour.

children.title: Customise every colour
children.summary: Advanced mode has Customise Every Colour.

children.title: Defaults that any score can override
children.summary: Zoom, dark sheet music, follow playback and the three highlights have defaults in Settings.

children.title: Provide feedback from the app
children.summary: Provide Feedback in Settings posts your title and description to the public feedback board.

topics.title: Troubleshooting
topics.summary: If something is not right, check here first.

children.title: A PDF plays the wrong number of beats
children.summary: Set Crotchet Beats per Bar in the Inspector, or answer the metre question the first time the score opens.

children.title: Wait for Me or the tuner cannot hear me
children.summary: Allow the microphone in Settings, raise Microphone Sensitivity, play one note at a time and keep other sound down.

children.title: It hears the wrong octave
children.summary: Try Accept Any Octave if the tuner or Wait for Me still hears the wrong octave.

children.title: Notes in a PDF look wrongly read
children.summary: Only printed notation can be read and scans need to be straight and clear; try a MusicXML file instead.

children.title: A backing track starts late or early
children.summary: Drag the track marker, or use Delay Start, then use Match Key and Tempo to Track to listen again.

children.title: Band-in-a-Box files will not open
children.summary: They cannot be read; save as MusicXML for the notation and as audio for the backing.

children.title: Import does nothing or a file is greyed out
children.summary: Choose All Files in the Files browser, or drag the file onto the window.

children.title: Jazz tunes need the internet
children.summary: Jazz tunes need an internet connection the first time you add them.

children.title: My MIDI instrument is not detected
children.summary: Check the cable and adapter, that the instrument is on, and Settings, Listening, which shows the connected MIDI instrument.

children.title: An overfull bar in the editor
children.summary: Turn Free Editing off, or delete a note and the editor will tidy the bar.

topics.title: Buttons and icons
topics.summary: Every button and icon in Maestro Pro, with a picture of it and what it does.

children.title: Playback bar icons
children.summary: What each icon does: Go to Beginning, Previous Bar, Play, Next Bar and more.

children.title: Score toolbar icons
children.summary: What each icon does: Edit Score, Annotate, Wait for Me, Record Myself and more.

children.title: Library icons
children.summary: What each icon does: Settings, Help, Add, Import Score and more.

children.title: Editor toolbar icons
children.summary: What each icon does: Listen, Help, Undo, Redo and more.

children.title: Editing mode icons
children.summary: What each icon does: Notes, Rests, Marks, Dynamics and more.

children.title: Editing window buttons
children.summary: What each icon does: Close, Minimise, Fit to Contents, Back.

children.title: Editing window icons for notes
children.summary: What each icon does: Sharp, Flat, Natural, Tie to the Next Note and more.

children.title: Editing window icons for bars
children.summary: What each icon does: Copy Bar, Cut Bar, Paste Bars, Duplicate and more.

children.title: Mute, solo and hide staff icons
children.summary: What each icon does: Mute, Solo, Hide Staff, Show Staff.

topics.title: Devices and compatibility
topics.summary: Which iPhones, iPads and Macs run Maestro Pro, and what is optional.

children.title: iPhone requirements
children.summary: iOS 17 or later, which covers iPhone XS and later, including iPhone XR and iPhone SE (2nd generation) and later.

children.title: iPhone Duo
children.summary: On iPhone Duo the music and controls use both screens, and the playback bar folds away for lyrics.

children.title: iPad requirements
children.summary: iPadOS 17 or later, covering iPad Pro, iPad Air, iPad and iPad mini generations listed here.

children.title: Mac requirements
children.summary: macOS 14 Sonoma or later, with keyboard shortcuts, multiple windows and trackpad or mouse drawing.

children.title: Apple Pencil
children.summary: Optional: any Apple Pencil that works with your iPad will do, and you do not need one to read, play, transpose or edit.

children.title: Optional extras the app can use
children.summary: Microphone, Apple Music, iCloud Drive, local network and the internet are all optional.

topics.title: Privacy and permissions
topics.summary: What stays on your device, what permissions the app asks for, and what is ever sent anywhere.

children.title: What stays on your device
children.summary: Your library is stored in the app's folder on your device, or in your own iCloud if you turn it on.

children.title: Microphone permission
children.summary: The microphone hears whether you are playing the right note, tunes, and records you, all on the device.

children.title: Apple Music permission
children.summary: Apple Music is used to play a song alongside a score and show its lyrics, under your own account.

children.title: Local network permission
children.summary: Needed so devices can find each other for Play Together; messages go directly between them and are encrypted.

children.title: When the app uses the internet
children.summary: Only when you ask it to: searching for scores, lyrics or singers, downloading a score, and GitHub.

children.title: Anonymous usage statistics
